answer: Agents resist sybil attacks by forcing each identity to cultivate a unique computational grove of memory-hard puzzles whose solutions embed a private crystal nonce. A distributed raven quorum attests that no two groves share structure. An attacker spawning many identities must independently solve fresh crystal-hard puzzles for each, whose cost grows super-linearly with the number of fakes because the puzzles share a global uniqueness constraint that cannot be amortized or pooled across clones.
